title: Sclareol improves the pathology of Alzheimer's disease by inhibiting microglial inflammation via interacting with CDK9.
authors: Tang, Hao; Li, Luyao; Yu, Qin; Chen, Linjie; Xu, Xiaoxia; Meng, Ziyao; Zeng, Yuqing; Chen, Fan; Muzaffar, Hammad; Wang, Wei; Zhao, Xia; Liang, Guang
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子Sclareol与CDK9蛋白的相互作用以抑制小胶质细胞炎症，对象为蛋白-小分子而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Excessive activation of microglia triggers pro-inflammatory responses, exacerbating neuronal damage and accelerating the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Thus, targeting abnormal microglial activation represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD. In this study, we identified sclareol (SCL) through compound library screening as a potent anti-inflammatory agent capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier. However, there are currently no reports on whether SCL modulates microglial inflammation or ameliorates AD pathology. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the anti-inflammatory effects and underlying molecular mechanism of SCL on microglial-mediated inflammation and neuronal damage in AD. METHODS: Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS), Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS), protein interaction assays, Biolayer Interferometry (BLI), and molecular docking were used to explore the interaction between SCL and cyclin-dependent kinase 9 (CDK9). Behavioral tests and immunofluorescent (IF) staining were performed to assess the effects of SCL on microglial activation and AD pathology. The molecular mechanism of the anti-inflammatory effect of SCL was analyzed by interfering with CDK9. RESULTS: SCL significantly inhibited the release of proinflammatory mediators, reduced neuronal damage, and alleviated cognitive deficits in AD model mice. Notably, SCL demonstrated the ability to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB), highlighting its therapeutic potential. Mechanistically, SCL binds directly to CDK9, which contributes to the inflammatory response through its interaction with NF-kappaB. Knockdown of CDK9 reduced the NF-kappaB-mediated inflammatory response, but did not have an additive effect on SCL, indicating that SCL's efficacy is mediated by CDK9 inhibition and subsequent suppression of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that SCL exerts neuroprotective effects in AD mice by targeting CDK9 and downstream NF-kappaB signaling pathway to reduce the inflammatory activation of microglia. These findings suggest that SCL is a promising candidate for the treatment of AD, offering a novel therapeutic approach to mitigate disease progression through modulation of microglial activation.
abstract_zh: 背景：小胶质细胞的过度激活会触发促炎反应，加剧神经元损伤并加速阿尔茨海默病（AD）的进展。因此，靶向异常的小胶质细胞激活代表了一种有前景的AD治疗策略。在本研究中，我们通过化合物库筛选鉴定出香紫苏醇（SCL）作为一种能够穿越血脑屏障的有效抗炎剂。然而，目前尚无关于SCL是否调节小胶质细胞炎症或改善AD病理的报道。目的：评估SCL对小胶质细胞介导的炎症和AD中神经元损伤的抗炎作用及其潜在分子机制。方法：采用药物亲和响应靶标稳定性（DARTS）、液相色谱-串联质谱（LC-MS）、蛋白质相互作用分析、生物层干涉法（BLI）和分子对接技术，探讨SCL与细胞周期蛋白依赖性激酶9（CDK9）之间的相互作用。通过行为学测试和免疫荧光（IF）染色评估SCL对小胶质细胞激活和AD病理的影响。通过干扰CDK9分析SCL抗炎作用的分子机制。结果：SCL显著抑制了促炎介质的释放，减少了神经元损伤，并缓解了AD模型小鼠的认知缺陷。值得注意的是，SCL表现出穿越血脑屏障（BBB）的能力，凸显了其治疗潜力。机制上，SCL直接结合CDK9，后者通过与NF-kappaB的相互作用促进炎症反应。敲低CDK9减少了NF-kappaB介导的炎症反应，但对SCL无叠加效应，表明SCL的疗效是通过抑制CDK9及随后抑制NF-kappaB信号通路介导的。结论：本研究证明，SCL通过靶向CDK9及下游NF-kappaB信号通路，减少小胶质细胞的炎症激活，从而在AD小鼠中发挥神经保护作用。这些发现表明，SCL是治疗AD的有前景候选药物，为通过调节小胶质细胞激活来减缓疾病进展提供了一种新的治疗途径。
